# Does the grid bind?

> An invariant audit of the claim that AI accelerator shipments are outrunning
> US grid energization. Verdict: the conclusion is about 80% likely to be right,
> and most of its stated reasons are wrong.

Audited 2026-09-18 against "What Happens When Chip Volume Doubles but the Grid
Does Not" (Dean Lee, dev.to, published the same day).

## Headline result

- P(stranding-forced regime) = 0.802 (Monte Carlo, n=500,000, seed 20260918)
- Median annual shortfall +1.66 GW/yr; median 20.7% of shipments arriving before power
- The exact interval classification of the same inputs returns UNDECIDED, so the
  probability is the honest form of the answer, not a point estimate
- 86 parameters, 45 of them hard evidence (MEASURED / FILED / OFFICIAL)
- 9/9 TLA+ model-checking runs matched their declared expected outcome

## What the audit found

- The article's dichotomy (strand it, or cannibalize the installed base) is
  actually a trichotomy with a computable boundary in shipped / energized /
  installed-base. TLC over every operator strategy.
- "Thirty percentage points" of ASP compression is an arithmetic error. Growth
  composes multiplicatively: (1+0.70)/(1+1.00) - 1 = -15%, exactly -3/20.
- The $673bn FY2028 revenue figure is not NVIDIA's; it is a news outlet's
  multiplication of an analyst consensus. "673" appears zero times in the 8-K,
  the 10-Q and the corrected transcript.
- GPU rental prices rose 32.5% off their December 2025 trough. A 2020-vintage
  A100 is appreciating. Electricity is 20% of cash marginal cost, not "largely" it.
- Straight-line book value depreciates FASTER than exponential resale decay; the
  curves cross at ~1.4 years, after which early retirement books a gain.
- 66.4% of the remaining variance sits in two quantities with no published
  measurement, neither of which the original article mentions.
